ruleName: Four-Ball: Wrong Number of Strokes Given
title: Giving the wrong number of strokes in four-ball
question: In a four-ball match, Daniel is asked by an opponent how many strokes he has taken. Daniel says three and his opponent concedes the hole. Daniel then realises he had actually taken four strokes. What is the ruling?

choices.text: The concession stands and there is no penalty.
Daniel is penalised two strokes but the concession stands.

explanation: In four-ball match play, if a player gives a wrong number of strokes taken that affects an opponent’s understanding of the match situation, their side loses the hole (Rule 23.8a(2)).
